static_traits.name: Li Ming
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends and classmates providing emotional support, but finds it hard to discuss the divorce and its impact on parenting with them
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problem experience, not yet received psychotherapy, No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, high cooperation, able to self-Reflect, Positive attitude, willing to try behavioral experiments

basic_info.main_problem: I have been troubled by the thought 'my child may see me as a bad dad because of the divorce', which brings me marked distress.
basic_info.core_demands: These thoughts are affecting my mental health and my relationship with my child. I want to work through these feelings and improve communication with my child.
growth_experiences: About a year ago, after divorcing my spouse, stress rose markedly, sleep and self-care were affected; my relationship with the children became tense, and I frequently experience guilt and sadness; academic performance declined slightly; although I have the emotional support of a few friends and classmates, it is hard to proactively talk about the divorce and its impact on parenting.

core_beliefs: Divorce means I failed; the children's pain is my fault

special_situations.event: Playing with the child in the park last weekend
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If children blame me in their hearts or are unhappy, it means I am a failure Father
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Being extra cautious in interactions, Repressing emotions and reducing play to avoid 'mistakes'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must be blaming me for the family no longer being whole; they think I am a bad dad

special_situations.event: Children asking 'why can't mom and dad be together'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the children raise the question of divorce, it means they think it is my fault
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately explains, and repeatedly reassures and guarantees 'we still love you'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They blame the divorce on me

special_situations.event: Before and after planning activities or spending time with the child
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If every interaction is not perfect, it proves I am a bad dad
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-plans, invests more time and attention to compensate and prove oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If this time is not good enough, they will hate me more and will distance themselves from me in the future

special_situations.event: Being alone Reflecting on fatherhood and family breakdown after Divorce
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only maintaining a complete family counts as a good father, otherwise one is a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proves oneself a good father by doubling companionship and care for the children
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Divorce means I am a bad father

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized by the children, maintain close connection, and be seen as a 'good father'
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being blamed or rejected by the children, afraid of being defined as a 'bad father'
defense_goal: Maintains security and recognition through excessive care and explanation
Staying restrained in interactions to avoid triggering dissatisfaction or blame

object_relations.self_representation: The guilty failed father who may be blamed
object_relations.object_representation: Judging or blaming one's own child

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When children ask why mom and dad cannot be together
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing children's understanding-seeking Questioning as blame and negation of oneself (transference: seeing the child as a judge)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in a calm, rational, explanatory tone, emphasizing facts and assurances, minimizing emotional self-exposure as much as possible, avoiding talking about feelings of self-blame.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: While playing with the child, guilt and sadness suddenly surge
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Misreading children's ordinary behavior as dissatisfaction or rejection (transference: interpreting others' positions Self-deprecatingly)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Lowers enthusiasm for interaction, maintains superficially normal communication, with a light and brief tone, avoiding expressing inner emotions.

manifestations: Divorce led to changes in family structure and increased distance in intimate relationships
Hard to discuss divorce and parenting feelings with friends and classmates
outcomes: Interactions with the children affected; estrangement appears

manifestations: Excessively tying self-worth to the evaluation of 'whether I am a good father'
Simplifying Divorce into negation of overall self-worth
outcomes: Declining academic focus; impaired quality of life

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Overly caring about the children's views and evaluations of oneself
Frequently blaming oneself as a 'bad dad', being overly cautious in interactions

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Becomes distant at the park due to guilt and plays less
Transforming impulses for closeness and play into self-Repression and Withdrawal

exception_events.target_problem: In situations of being with children or planning activities, the client usually falls into the thought 'the children blame me', produces guilt and sadness, and becomes distant in the interaction.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last weekend at the park, the children focused on playing and looked happy, showing no signs of dissatisfaction or blame; the client noticed these positive reactions.
exception_events.reason: Different situation: outdoor play, children's natural positive feedback; different approach: the client invested in companionship and tried observational recording; supporting clue: the children's present joy and engagement as real evidence.

positive_force: Strong fathering motivation and ongoing actions of accompanying the child (proactively arranging activities, investing time)
Willing to seek counseling and participate in behavioral experiments, with self-Reflection ability
Able to explain the divorce in a gentle way and give the children stable emotional comfort
negative_force: Mind-reading and future-predicting tendencies, over-interpreting children's reactions as blame
Guilt and sadness lead to declines in sleep and self-care
Struggling to discuss Divorce and parenting troubles with friends and classmates, limited use of Social support

target_behavior.behavior: When with the children, distance appears and play decreases (interaction enthusiasm declines)
antecedent: Activities with the child (e.g. at the park)
Before or during planning activities with the children
target_behavior.core_reason: Interpreting children's Questioning and ordinary behavior as blaming oneself, triggering guilt and Anxiety, thus reducing interaction investment
target_behavior.function: Escaping the emotion of being blamed and reducing Anxiety (negative Reinforcement)
target_behavior.consequence: Declining parent-child interaction quality, tenser relationship, further Reinforcing negative beliefs

target_behavior.behavior: Sleep impaired and Decreased attention (emotional physiological and behavioral reactions)
antecedent: Repeatedly thinking about the divorce and the children's views of oneself
Persistently ruminating negative thoughts after spending time with the children
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing and mind reading lead to persistent negative rumination and heightened arousal
target_behavior.function: Trying to prevent negative evaluation through worry (maladaptive Self-monitoring)
target_behavior.consequence: Academic performance slightly declines, daily self-care is affected, fatigue worsens
